We are a small, fictional editorial team with a simple belief: the useful ideas are often hiding in ordinary things.

Take a closer look

A well-made tool. A clear explanation. A quiet moment that changes how you see the rest of the day. Fieldnotes collects perspectives on design, engineering, and the everyday.

Stay curious

@props(title:text)
THE STUDIO

A small studio.
A long view.

We bring calm thinking and a hands-on approach to the spaces you call your own.

Built around people

Every project begins with a conversation, not a drawing. How do you spend your mornings? Where does the light fall? What would make an ordinary day a little better?

We work from those details outward, using natural materials and clear ideas to create places that will grow with you.

Courtyard House

A home turned inward toward a quiet garden. Deep window reveals, limewashed walls, and a generous threshold connect every room to the outdoors.

Hillside Retreat

A compact timber house follows the shape of its landscape. A single broad roof creates a sheltered edge for watching the weather pass.

SAY HELLO

Good things start
with a conversation.

Run the browser verification

Checks node identity, input focus and caret, selection, sorting, filtering, and adding/removing rows on this actual DOM. The live site also checks a fresh Neo server render.

Not run yet.
What this measures

Windowing limits DOM work to visible rows plus overscan and a pinned focused row. Models retain notes, selection and counters outside the window. The live loop changes 10% of values every 100ms; Update every row changes all values. Focused rows keep their node and caret; offscreen rows are recreated from their models. Filtering intentionally removes nonmatching rows. The optional render=full query is an unvirtualized diagnostic reference and can stall. Blank-frame and focus checks do not prove the absence of every possible visual artifact; long-frame measurements provide an additional signal. Patch timings measure JavaScript DOM work, not browser layout and paint. The steady p95 excludes structural changes and the deliberately slow full-redraw comparison.
